svg.title: Simplified mock-up of the Copilot Studio form for adding an A2A agent, filled in for Cedar Dispatch Advisor
svg.desc: A simplified drawing, not a product screenshot, of the Agents page of the Cedar Service Assistant after Add agent and A2A agent. Fields from top to bottom: Endpoint URL https://ca-cedar-advisor-dev.example/a2a, the message endpoint and not the card URL; Name Cedar Dispatch Advisor and Description, filled in from the agent card; Authentication OAuth 2.0; Client ID of the app registration Cedar Copilot Studio A2A client; Client secret, stored in the connection and taken from Key Vault, never written in a file; Authorization URL and Token URL and Refresh URL on login.microsoftonline.com for the tenant ID. Buttons Save and then Add and configure. Five callouts on the right explain: 1 the endpoint is the message endpoint /a2a, the card is read from /.well-known; 2 the description is filled in from the card and decides routing, so it says what the agent does not do; 3 OAuth 2.0 with Entra ID, never None or an API key; 4 the secret comes from Key Vault and lives in the connection, not in Git; 5 after saving, copy the redirect URI shown by the connection into the client app registration, then sign in and test.
svg.text: Add agent → A2A agent (simplified; labels may differ in your tenant)
Explains which subcontractors Cedar's dispatch rules rank first for
one work order and why others are not eligible. It doesn't give work
order status or service level figures and doesn't dispatch.
Message endpoint (/a2a), not the card URL.
Filled in from the card. The orchestrator
routes by it: say what it does NOT do, so
it doesn't overlap Work order status.
Entra ID through OAuth 2.0; never None,
never an API key (ADR-018, rule AG-10).
Secret from Key Vault, typed here once;
it lives in the connection, not in Git.
After Save: copy the redirect URI the
connection shows into the client app
registration, then sign in and test.
